clue.text: Predator combining first-rate vision with wisdom?

parts.note: keen sight is called eagle eyes, so the bird stands for excellent vision
the owl is the traditional symbol of wisdom

explanation.surface: A hunting creature blessed with both sharp eyes and great wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: This large nocturnal bird of prey hunts small mammals, so it is a predator.

clue.text: Remarkable example among gramophone records

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the run of words gramophone records

explanation.surface: A standout item turns up in a collection of old gramophone discs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the hidden run, across the end of gramophone and the start of records.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a unique or outstanding person or thing, a one-off.

clue.text: Don't abandon tower

explanation.surface: An appeal not to give up the castle tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is not to abandon it; the strongest central tower of a castle is also called by this name.

clue.text: Robbed, remained strong

explanation.surface: Someone mugged who nevertheless stayed firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim of an armed robbery has been stuck up; a structure or person that lasted without collapsing has stood firm.

clue.text: Like part of skull a pirate damaged and left

indicators.note: damaged suggests the words a pirate are broken and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A buccaneer's head wound, with the pirate then departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges A PIRATE into PARIETA, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The parietal bones form the sides and roof of the cranium, so the adjective describes that region of the skull.

clue.text: Gives support to your health

explanation.surface: Encouragement offered alongside a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators who shout encouragement are supporting a team; raising a glass with a toast to someone's health uses the same word.

clue.text: Ham and tripe

explanation.surface: A menu listing pork and offal.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like food, but 'tripe' here means nonsense, the puzzle's running theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork from the hind leg is a ham steak of this kind; as British slang the word also means rubbish talk.

clue.text: Is unhappy with endless confusion about work

indicators.note: about places the shortened word around the piece for work
endless means the final letter of the word for confusion is cut off

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable because of an unending muddle concerning their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final letter of the confusion word, and 'about' wraps the shortened word round the abbreviation for an opus.
explanation.definitionFit: To sulk around feeling low and listless is to be unhappy in a gloomy way.

clue.text: It helps give a clearer view of English trees

definitions.text: It helps give a clearer view

parts.note: yew is a kind of tree
ash is another kind of tree

explanation.surface: Something that sharpens the view of the English woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trees' gives two species, one after the other. The answer also fits the theme as a word for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion for rinsing the eyes clears them so one can see better; it is also slang for humbug.

clue.text: Report some rejected as piffle

parts.note: a clap is a loud report, as of thunder or a gun

indicators.note: rejected tells the solver the word for some is turned back to front

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: A news report partly dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' suggests a news story but means a bang; 'rejected' turns the word for some back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words for silly, pretentious talk with no substance.

clue.text: Meaningless talk to motivate left

parts.note: to drive someone is to motivate or push them on

explanation.surface: Empty chatter meant to inspire someone who has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly, rambling speech with no sense in it is nonsense, the theme of the grid.

clue.text: Absurdity of jokes with strong impact

parts.note: cod is British slang for a hoax or joke, so cods are jokes
a wallop is a heavy blow

explanation.surface: A ridiculous situation made of gags that hit hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cod' as a British word for a spoof or hoax gives the first part; the result is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for nonsense or something utterly ridiculous.

clue.text: Beheaded villain on stage in the past

indicators.note: beheaded tells the solver to cut off the first letter of the name

parts.note: Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello

explanation.surface: A stage villain who lost his head long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' removes the I from IAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a period of time, as in years before now, it means in the past.

clue.text: Woman left university with people of intelligence

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency, people who gather intelligence

explanation.surface: A woman quits her college to join some brainy types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people of intelligence' means spies, not clever folk.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as in the opera heroine of Lammermoor.

clue.text: Casual form of address disturbed host

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of host are stirred into a different order

explanation.surface: A slangy greeting rattles the person throwing the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges HOST. The answer also means nonsense, the theme. In Britain the word is a jokey way to address a man whose name you don't know.
explanation.definitionFit: A matey British way of addressing a stranger, like mate or pal.

clue.text: Cargo of fruit drinks and moonshine

parts.note: a load is a cargo carried by a vehicle
taken as written
a cobbler is an iced drink of wine or sherry with fruit and sugar

explanation.surface: A shipment of fruity cocktails and illicit spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moonshine' looks like bootleg liquor to match the drinks, but here it means nonsense. COBBLERS is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine means foolish talk, and this British phrase means utter rubbish.

clue.text: Was charming and contested verdict

explanation.surface: A charmer who also challenged the court's ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attractive pleased people; a party who took a ruling to a higher court challenged the judgement.

clue.text: Order one diamond, say

explanation.surface: Commanding a single gem, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, calling 'one diamond' is a typical call in the auction.
explanation.definitionFit: To command someone is to tell them to do something; in bridge each call such as one diamond is an offer in the auction.

clue.text: Doesn't consider measures inaccurate

parts.note: rules are measuring sticks, so measures
a calculation that is out is wrong

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the yardsticks as wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude a possibility is to refuse to consider it.

clue.text: Losing throw of dice in run accepted by better

indicators.note: accepted by means the letter for run is taken inside the word for better

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A gambler's bad roll, which the man placing the bet takes in his stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as a gambler, but it is the verb meaning outdo. In the dice game craps, a two, three or twelve on the first roll loses.
explanation.definitionFit: In craps, a first roll of two, three or twelve loses the bet; the word is also slang for rubbish.

clue.text: Rob him violently, getting diamonds

indicators.note: violently hints the letters of rob him are roughly shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A violent mugging that yields precious stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' means the geometric shapes, not gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the four-sided figure with equal sides, the shape known as a diamond or lozenge.

clue.text: Paddle frantically with fool, an American one

indicators.note: frantically suggests the letters of paddle and fool are thrown together in a mad jumble

explanation.surface: Someone paddles wildly alongside a fool from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to the theme: the answer is a piece of nonsense, an American slang word for it.
explanation.definitionFit: US slang for nonsense or balderdash, so a variety of rubbish from across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Trees found around most of the inlets in Scotland

indicators.note: found around means the trees enclose the shortened word

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Woodland ringing the sea lochs of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the clue's own word 'the', and 'found around' sets the conifers round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots term for an estuary or long arm of the sea, like the Forth.

clue.text: Sort of canoe -Indian, for example

indicators.note: sort of tells the solver to sort, or rearrange, the letters of canoe

explanation.surface: A kind of canoe, an Indian one perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a type of canoe, but it is the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one of the world's great bodies of salt water, alongside the Atlantic and Pacific.

clue.text: Worthless speech made before the balloon goes up

definitions.text: made before the balloon goes up

explanation.surface: Empty talk delivered just before the balloon rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty boastful talk is nonsense; a hot-air balloon is filled with heated gas before it can rise.

clue.text: Bull has no ring, repeatedly removed from nose

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: repeatedly means the shortened nose is written twice in a row
removed from says the ring letter is taken out of nose

parts.note: taken as written
O is a ring, from its round shape

explanation.surface: A bull whose nose ring has been taken off again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bull with a nose ring, but 'Bull' is the definition; 'removed from' takes the ring letter out of nose, and 'repeatedly' writes that remainder twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is slang for rubbish talk, short for a coarser word.

clue.text: New king, old emperor

parts.note: ER is Edward Rex, King Edward's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A newly crowned king beside an ancient emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman ruler said to have fiddled while Rome burned was emperor from AD 54 to 68.

clue.text: Top people getting no answer to any across clue

parts.note: taken as written
every across answer in this grid means nonsense, and BS is slang initials for exactly that

explanation.surface: Important people who can't solve any of the across clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The across answers are all words for nonsense, and BS, short for a coarse word, is one more.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for wealthy or upper-class folk, the toffs.

clue.text: Empty talk — some ramble therein

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Idle chatter as someone rambles on inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals letters taken from inside 'ramble therein'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots and northern English word for foolish chatter, gabbling at length.

clue.text: Rubbish from bed taken with hesitation

parts.note: a bunk is a narrow bed
um is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Nonsense coming from someone hesitating in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or claptrap; the word derives from a long-winded speech for Buncombe County.
